title: Tenant affinity inversion during controller rolling upgrades causing sudden dedicated capacity cliffs
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary: During a staggered controller rolling upgrade in us-west-2 on 2026-03-10 we observed multiple dedicated reserved pools suddenly drop available capacity for a subset of tenants. Impacted tenants experienced elevated tail latency and 503s for short windows (30-120s). Several customers escalated via support: BrightLane reported timeout-triggered failovers; HelixRisk saw degraded throughput for critical jobs; OrbitPay experienced transient transaction retries.

What happened (reproduction):
- Step 1: Start a controlled rolling upgrade of controller replicas (node images updated to runtime-controller v2.14.1).
- Step 2: Leadership flapped once during upgrade due to a transient etcd latency spike.
- Step 3: The new leader applied an affinity reconciliation pass that wrote affinity keys without the previous epoch prefix in a short window where allocator instances had already garbage-collected stale local affinity caches.
- Step 4: Allocator interpreted the missing/empty epoch-prefixed keys as a deliberate inversion signal (legacy fallback behavior) and assigned several tenants to cold-boot pools, triggering immediate reserved-pool headroom consumption and burst-credit exhaustion.

Observed signals / logs:
- allocator WARN: "affinity key missing, applying inverted affinity fallback" (controller-epoch 0 -> had been >42 previously)
- autoscaler metrics: reserved_pool_available_tokens[pool_id] drop by ~85% for affected pools (duration 45-90s)
- burst_credit: debit spikes with no subsequent replenishment events for same tenants for ~2 minutes
- grafana panels: sudden queued_requests and allocation_failures correlated with controller leader election timestamp

Immediate customer impact:
- Increased tail latency up to 1.8s median -> 12s p99 for generation endpoints on dedicated pools.
- 502/503 errors for short bursts for customers with tight SLAs.
- One customer (OrbitPay) triggered secondary system retries causing downstream duplicate processing (customer mitigated via their idempotency keys).

Root cause hypothesis:
- Race between controller affinity reconciliation and allocator's local cache GC combined with a legacy fallback behavior that treats absent epoch-prefixed keys as an inverted-affinity instruction.
- A config change in v2.14.1 accidentally lowered the controller write batch timeout, increasing the probability that a write occurred while allocators were in mid-GC.

Mitigation implemented (hotfix):
1) Rolled a targeted hotpatch to controller: ensure affinity writes are epoch-prefixed and include a leader-validated commit stamp. Hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controller/pull/11234
2) Temporarily extended allocator local-cache grace window from 15s -> 120s in production via feature flag (allocator.gc_grace_window=120s) to reduce replay windows during rolling upgrades.
3) Manual reconciliation script run: tools/reconcile_affinity.sh to reapply correct epoched affinity for affected tenants; validated by memory snapshot and allocation logs.

Permanent fix plan (implementation):
- Code changes: (a) make affinity reconciliation idempotent and reject inverted-fallback interpretation unless explicit inversion flag present; (b) implement epoch-atomic writes with compare-and-swap semantics in controller; (c) autoscaler to maintain a temporary reserve (N=3 slots or 7% of pool capacity) during leader election windows.
- Testing: unit tests for epoch handling, chaos tests simulating leader flip + GC, integration test that runs a mini-scheduler upgrade while validating no affinity inversion occurs.
- Rollout: Canary the controller hotfix to 10% of controllers, observe for 48 hours, then progressive rollout. Autoscaler reserve will be enabled behind a toggle for 72h canary before global enable.

Runbook and monitoring updates:
- New runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/dedicated-affinity-inversion (created)
- Grafana dashboards to add: controller_write_latency, allocator_gc_events, affinity_epoch_mismatch_count
- Pager triggers: allocate_failure_rate > 0.5% for 5m and reserved_pool_token_drop_rate > 50% for 1m.

Communication and customer work: 
- Sent incident summary and short-term mitigation to BrightLane, HelixRisk, OrbitPay on 2026-03-11; follow-up with timeline for permanent fix and compensating credits.
- Support templates updated for common troubleshooting steps (restart-only-not-recommend unless hotpatch applied).

Follow-ups / postmortem action items:
- (A1) Replace inverted-fallback behavior in allocator with explicit opt-in only (owner: Maia Chen, estimate 3)
- (A2) Revert temporary allocator.gc_grace_window tweak after controller patch is fully rolled out and validated (owner: SRE, estimate 1)
- (A3) Add automated preflight check that prevents controller rolling upgrade if allocator cluster GC rate > threshold (owner: Platform Eng, estimate 5)
- (A4) Create a synthetic workload that continuously validates reserved-pool invariants during control-plane upgrades (owner: QA, estimate 5)

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- Canary rollout shows no affinity inversion events for 7 days
- Reserved-pool allocation failure rate returns to baseline (<0.05%) and stays stable for 48 hours post-global rollout
- Runbook reviewed and signed off by oncall and SRE

Notes: This ticket covers the investigation, hotpatch tracking, runbook creation, and follow-up engineering changes. A separate ticket will track long-term chaos-testing and synthetic workload (see dependencies).
